questions.q: What makes teams structurally different from sharing rules?
options: Teams attach access to one specific record; sharing rules grant access to a whole population of records at once
Teams can only be used on custom objects, while sharing rules only work on standard objects
Teams always grant Read/Write access, while sharing rules can only grant Read Only
Teams are evaluated by criteria, while sharing rules are evaluated by ownership only
questions.explain: Sharing rules operate on populations — everyone owned by a role, everyone matching criteria. Teams are a list of people attached to one specific record, each with an individual access level and role on that record.

questions.q: A sales engineer needs access to exactly three specific Opportunities this quarter, and no others. Which mechanism fits this requirement best?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule
Lowering the object's organization-wide default
An Opportunity Team added to each of those three specific records
A role hierarchy change
questions.explain: Because the requirement is tied to specific individual records rather than a describable population, an Opportunity Team on exactly those three records grants precise access without affecting any other record.

questions.q: A rep updates their personal default Opportunity Team this week. What happens to the team already attached to an Opportunity they created last month?
options: It updates automatically to match the new default team
It stays exactly as it was — default team changes only apply to new records created after the change
The Opportunity is automatically re-shared with everyone in the org
The old Opportunity's team is deleted entirely
questions.explain: A default team is only a template copied onto new records at creation time. Changing it going forward has no retroactive effect on team membership already baked into existing records.

questions.q: Why don't teams trigger a sharing recalculation job the way sharing rules do?
options: Because team membership is just data on the record itself — there's no rule to re-evaluate, so changes take effect instantly without a background job
Because teams are disabled by default in every Salesforce org
Because teams only work on objects with Public Read/Write organization-wide defaults
Because Salesforce recalculates team membership nightly on a fixed schedule
questions.explain: Sharing rules depend on recalculation because they're a rule being re-evaluated against changing data. A team's membership is simply stored on the record, so adding or removing someone takes effect immediately with no recalculation job involved.

questions.q: An architect notices someone recommending 'add this same five-person team to every Opportunity this rep owns.' What should the architect flag about this approach?
options: Nothing — this is exactly what Opportunity Teams are designed for
This is actually a population-level sharing requirement wearing a team-shaped disguise, and should be redesigned as a sharing rule or role-hierarchy change instead
This requires disabling Grant Access Using Hierarchies first
This can only be done through Apex managed sharing, never through a team
questions.explain: Teams are designed for record-specific collaboration, not as a substitute for population-level access. A fixed team being applied to every record a given owner creates is really a sharing-rule or role-hierarchy requirement, and should be modeled as one so the access doesn't depend on someone remembering to populate a team on every record.
